q: 'Indumati', published in the year 1900 and regarded as the first short story in Hindi, was written by:
e: 'Indumati', published in 1900 in the magazine Saraswati and written by Kishorilal Goswami, is regarded as the first short story in Hindi.

q: The celebrated Hindi poet Suryakant Tripathi is popularly known by his pen-name:
e: Suryakant Tripathi, the great Chhayavad poet, is known by his pen-name 'Nirala'. 'Dinkar' is Ramdhari Singh and 'Hariaudh' is Ayodhya Singh Upadhyay.

q: The first woman writer to receive the Jnanpith Award was:
e: The Bengali novelist Ashapurna Devi was the first woman writer to receive the Jnanpith Award; women litterateurs like Amrita Pritam and Mahadevi Varma were honoured later.

q: Saint-poet Kabir is traditionally regarded as a disciple of:
e: Saint-poet Kabir, the weaver of Varanasi, is traditionally regarded as a disciple of Swami Ramananda, the Vaishnava teacher who preached devotion in the language of the people.

q: The 'Ashtachhap' group of medieval devotional poets, of whom Surdas was the most celebrated, was associated with the Pushtimarg tradition founded by:
e: The Ashtachhap poets, of whom Surdas was the most celebrated, belonged to the Pushtimarg tradition of Krishna devotion founded by Vallabhacharya.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Consolidated Fund" is:
e: 'Sanchit' means accumulated or pooled, so the Consolidated Fund, into which all revenues of the Government flow, is Sanchit Nidhi. Lok Lekha is the Public Account.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Contingency Fund" is:
e: 'Aakasmikta' means a sudden unforeseen contingency, so the Contingency Fund kept for urgent unforeseen expenditure is Aakasmikta Nidhi.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Public Account" is:
e: In the Public Account the Government acts as banker or trustee for others' money; this account is Lok Lekha. Sanchit Nidhi is the Consolidated Fund and Koshagar the Treasury.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Appropriation" is:
e: Viniyog means allocation or application of funds authorised by the legislature, so an Appropriation is Viniyog, as in Viniyog Adhiniyam, the Appropriation Act. Anudan is a grant.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Vote on Account" is:
e: A Vote on Account, the grant obtained for part of the year pending the passing of the full budget, is called Lekhanudan. Poorak Anudan is a supplementary grant.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Balance Sheet" is:
e: A Balance Sheet sets assets and liabilities face to face in balance, hence Tulan Patra, from 'Tulan' meaning comparison or balance.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Bye-laws" is:
e: Bye-laws are subsidiary rules framed by an authority under a parent Act, hence Upvidhi - 'Up' meaning sub or subsidiary and 'Vidhi' law. Adhiniyam is an Act.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Manual" is:
e: A Manual is a book collecting the rules and procedure on a subject, hence Niyamavali, a collection (Avali) of rules (Niyam). Samhita is a code.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Statistics" is:
e: Sankhyiki, derived from 'Sankhya' meaning number, is the science of statistics - the collection, presentation and analysis of numerical data. Sankalan is mere compilation.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Report" is:
e: Prativedan is the formal term for a report submitted by an officer, committee or commission. Vivaran is a description or statement, and Tippan a noting or comment.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Loan" is:
e: Rin is money borrowed which has to be repaid, i.e., a loan or debt. Agrim is an advance, Jama a deposit and Vasuli the recovery of dues.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Treasury" is:
e: The Treasury, the office where government money is received, kept and paid out, is Koshagar - Kosh (fund or treasure) plus Agar (house). Tijori is a safe.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Stores" is:
e: Materials and supplies held in stock for use are Stores, called Bhandar. Godam is the warehouse building itself and Samagri means material in general.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Time Table" is:
e: A time table sets out timings in an ordered table, hence Samay Sarini - Samay (time) plus Sarini (table or series). Dincharya is a daily routine.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Index" is:
e: An index, the alphabetical list that points to the contents of a book or file, is Anukramanika. Anusuchi is a schedule or list and Parishisht an appendix.

q: 'Saket', the celebrated Hindi epic poem centred on the character of Urmila, was written by:
e: 'Saket', the celebrated epic poem centred on Urmila, the devoted wife of Lakshmana, was written by Maithili Sharan Gupt.

q: 'Shekhar: Ek Jivani', the celebrated Hindi novel, was written by:
e: 'Shekhar: Ek Jivani', the celebrated psychological and experimental novel, was written by Agyeya, the pen-name of Sachchidananda Hirananda Vatsyayan.

q: 'Gunahon Ka Devta', the celebrated Hindi novel, was written by:
e: 'Gunahon Ka Devta', the much-loved novel of the love of Chander and Sudha, was written by Dharamvir Bharati.

q: 'Raag Darbari', the celebrated satirical Hindi novel, was written by:
e: 'Raag Darbari', the celebrated satirical novel exposing the politics and administration of a village, was written by Shrilal Shukla.

q: 'Tamas', the celebrated Hindi novel depicting the Partition of India, was written by:
e: 'Tamas', the powerful novel portraying the communal violence that accompanied the Partition of India, was written by Bhisham Sahni.

q: 'Chitralekha', the celebrated Hindi novel, was written by:
e: 'Chitralekha', the celebrated philosophical novel debating sin and virtue through the lives of its characters, was written by Bhagwati Charan Verma.

q: 'Usne Kaha Tha', the celebrated Hindi short story, was written by:
e: 'Usne Kaha Tha', the celebrated story of a soldier's sacrifice set in the First World War, was written by Chandradhar Sharma Guleri.

q: 'Eidgah', the celebrated Hindi short story, was written by:
e: 'Eidgah', the touching story of the child Hamid who buys a pair of tongs for his grandmother, is a famous short story of Munshi Premchand.

q: 'Dhruvaswamini', the celebrated Hindi play, was written by:
e: 'Dhruvaswamini', the celebrated historical play on the Gupta queen Dhruvaswamini, was written by Jaishankar Prasad.

q: Sumitranandan Pant was awarded the Jnanpith Award for his poetry collection:
e: Sumitranandan Pant was awarded the Jnanpith Award for his poetry collection 'Chidambara'. 'Yama' is Mahadevi Varma's work and 'Urvashi' is Dinkar's.

q: 'Jhootha Sach', the celebrated Hindi novel depicting the Partition of India, was written by:
e: 'Jhootha Sach', the celebrated two-part novel depicting the Partition of India and the life of the refugees after it, was written by Yashpal.

q: 'Andha Yug', the celebrated Hindi verse play, was written by:
e: 'Andha Yug', the celebrated verse play set in the aftermath of the Mahabharata war, was written by Dharamvir Bharati.

q: The Chhattisgarhi dialect belongs to which group of Hindi dialects?
e: Chhattisgarhi, spoken in the Chhattisgarh region, belongs to the Eastern Hindi group of dialects, along with Awadhi and Bagheli.

q: Which of the following languages belongs to the Bihari group of languages?
e: Maithili, along with Bhojpuri and Magahi, belongs to the Bihari group. Awadhi and Bagheli are Eastern Hindi dialects, while Braj is Western Hindi.

q: The Kharoshthi script, used in ancient India, was written:
e: The ancient Kharoshthi script of north-western India was written from right to left, whereas Brahmi and its descendant Devanagari run from left to right.

q: The inscriptions (edicts) of Emperor Ashoka are mostly written in which language?
e: Ashoka spread his edicts in Prakrit, the language understood by the common people of his time, engraving them in the Brahmi and Kharoshthi scripts.

q: 'Ashtadhyayi', the celebrated treatise on Sanskrit grammar, was composed by:
e: The 'Ashtadhyayi', the foundational treatise on Sanskrit grammar arranged in about four thousand sutras, was composed by the great grammarian Panini.

q: The original 'Ramayana' of Valmiki is composed in which language?
e: Valmiki composed the original Ramayana in Sanskrit, in the shloka metre; the later Ramcharitmanas of Tulsidas is in Awadhi.

q: The Fort William College at Calcutta, associated with the development of Hindi prose, was established in the year 1800 by:
e: Fort William College at Calcutta was established in 1800 by Governor-General Lord Wellesley to train British civil servants in Indian languages and laws.

q: 'Prem Sagar', an early prose work in Khari Boli Hindi produced at the Fort William College, was written by:
e: 'Prem Sagar', the early Khari Boli prose work on the Krishna story produced at Fort William College, was written by Lallu Lal.

q: The word 'Urdu' is derived from a Turkish word which means:
e: The word 'Urdu' comes from the Turkish word 'ordu', meaning an army or army camp; the language grew up in and around the military camps and bazaars.

q: 'Sarnami', a form of Hindi spoken by the Indian diaspora, is spoken mainly in:
e: Sarnami is the form of Hindi carried by Indian indentured labourers to Suriname in South America, where their descendants still speak it.

q: The language of the subordinate (district) courts in the State of Chhattisgarh is:
e: The language of the subordinate courts in Chhattisgarh is Hindi, which is also the official language of the State.

q: Under Article 348(1) of the Constitution, the authoritative texts of all orders, rules, regulations and bye-laws issued under the Constitution or under any law made by Parliament or the Legislature of a State shall be in:

options.C: The official language of the State concerned

e: Article 348(1) lays down that the authoritative texts of all Bills, Acts, orders, rules, regulations and bye-laws shall be in the English language, until Parliament provides otherwise.

q: The Central Translation Bureau (Kendriya Anuvad Bureau) functions as a subordinate office of the:

options.B: Legislative Department, Ministry of Law and Justice
options.C: Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs

e: The Central Translation Bureau, which translates codes, manuals and other non-statutory material, functions as a subordinate office of the Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs.

q: The Hindi Sahitya Sammelan, founded in the year 1910, has its headquarters at:
e: The Hindi Sahitya Sammelan, founded in 1910 for the promotion of Hindi, has its headquarters at Prayagraj, where its museum and library are also located.

q: The celebrated Hindi magazine 'Hans' was founded by:
e: The celebrated Hindi literary magazine 'Hans' was founded by Munshi Premchand, the greatest name in Hindi fiction, and remains a leading literary journal.

q: The celebrated Hindi magazine 'Saraswati' was first published in the year:
e: 'Saraswati', the celebrated magazine that shaped modern Hindi literature under editors like Mahavir Prasad Dwivedi, was first published in 1900.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Both Hindi and Urdu have developed from the Khari Boli dialect.
2. The Kanauji dialect belongs to the Eastern Hindi group of dialects.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is true: both Hindi and Urdu developed from the Khari Boli dialect of the Delhi-Meerut region. Statement 2 is false: Kanauji belongs to the Western Hindi group, not Eastern Hindi. Hence 1 only.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Tripitaka, the canonical literature of Buddhism, is written in the Pali language.
2. The Jain Agamas are written in the Sanskrit language.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is true: the Tripitaka, the canonical literature of Buddhism, is written in Pali. Statement 2 is false: the Jain Agamas are written in Ardhamagadhi Prakrit, not Sanskrit. Hence 1 only.

q: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with regard to the chapters of Part XVII of the Constitution?

options.A: Chapter I — Language of the Supreme Court and the High Courts
options.D: Chapter IV — Language of the Union

e: Part XVII of the Constitution is arranged as Chapter I - Language of the Union (Articles 343-344), Chapter II - Regional Languages (Articles 345-347), Chapter III - Language of the Supreme Court, High Courts, etc. (Articles 348-349) and Chapter IV - Special Directives (Articles 350-351), so only the Chapter II pairing is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 344 provides for the constitution of an Official Language Commission at the expiration of five years from the commencement of the Constitution, and thereafter at the expiration of ten years from such commencement.
2. Only one Official Language Commission has been constituted under Article 344 so far.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Article 344(1) requires the President to constitute an Official Language Commission at the expiration of five years from commencement of the Constitution and thereafter at the expiration of ten years. Only one such Commission, the Kher Commission of 1955, has been constituted so far, so both statements are correct.

q: Which of the following statements about the Committee of Parliament on Official Language is FALSE?

options.B: Its Chairman is nominated by the President
options.C: Its members are elected in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote
options.D: It reviews the progress made in the use of Hindi for the official purposes of the Union and reports to the President

e: The Committee of Parliament on Official Language under Section 4 of the Official Languages Act, 1963 has 30 members elected by proportional representation by single transferable vote, and its Chairman is elected by the members from amongst themselves, not nominated by the President; it reviews progress in the use of Hindi and reports to the President.

q: Which of the following is the correct chronological order of the events relating to the Official Language Policy of the Union?

options.A: Presidential Order — First Official Language Commission — Official Languages Act — Official Language Rules
options.B: Official Languages Act — First Official Language Commission — Presidential Order — Official Language Rules
options.C: First Official Language Commission — Presidential Order — Official Languages Act — Official Language Rules
options.D: First Official Language Commission — Official Languages Act — Official Language Rules — Presidential Order

e: The first Official Language Commission was appointed in 1955 and reported in 1956; the Presidential Order on its recommendations, after the Parliamentary Committee report, came in 1960; the Official Languages Act followed in 1963 and the Official Language Rules in 1976, giving the order Commission, Order, Act, Rules.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. An employee who has passed the Matriculation or an equivalent examination with Hindi as one of the subjects is deemed to have acquired proficiency in Hindi.
2. An employee who declares himself to be in possession of working knowledge of Hindi is deemed to have acquired working knowledge of Hindi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, passing Matriculation with Hindi as a subject gives working knowledge, not proficiency; proficiency requires Hindi as the medium of examination or an equivalent standard. A self-declaration of working knowledge is expressly accepted for working knowledge, so only statement 2 is correct.

q: An employee shall NOT be deemed to have acquired working knowledge of Hindi merely because he has:

options.A: Passed the Pragya examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme
options.B: Passed the Matriculation examination with Hindi as the medium of examination
options.C: Declared himself to be in possession of working knowledge of Hindi
options.D: Passed the Prabodh examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme

e: Working knowledge under Rule 10 of the Official Language Rules, 1976 is acquired by passing Matriculation with Hindi as a subject, passing Pragya under the Hindi Teaching Scheme, or by self-declaration. Prabodh is only the elementary course below Pragya, so passing Prabodh alone does not confer working knowledge.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Tulu is not included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution.
2. Dogri was added to the Eighth Schedule by the Constitution (92nd Amendment) Act, 2003.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The Eighth Schedule contains 22 languages and Tulu is not among them. Dogri, along with Bodo, Maithili and Santhali, was added by the Constitution (92nd Amendment) Act, 2003, so both statements are correct.

q: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with regard to the constitutional amendments relating to the Eighth Schedule?

options.A: Constitution (21st Amendment) Act — Konkani added to the Eighth Schedule
options.B: Constitution (71st Amendment) Act — Bodo added to the Eighth Schedule
options.C: Constitution (92nd Amendment) Act — Sindhi added to the Eighth Schedule
options.D: Constitution (96th Amendment) Act — the name 'Oriya' in the Eighth Schedule replaced by 'Odia'

e: The 21st Amendment (1967) added Sindhi, the 71st Amendment (1992) added Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali, and the 92nd Amendment (2003) added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali. The 96th Amendment Act, 2011 replaced the name Oriya with Odia in the Eighth Schedule, so only that pairing is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. 'Rules' issued by a Central Government office are among the documents specified in Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963 which are required to be issued in both Hindi and English.
2. The service book of a Government employee is also among the documents so specified in Section 3(3).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963 lists documents such as resolutions, general orders, rules, notifications, reports, contracts, licences, permits and tender forms, which must be issued in both Hindi and English. A service book is not in that list, so only statement 1 is correct.

q: Article 343(3) of the Constitution empowers Parliament to provide by law, even after the expiration of the initial period of fifteen years, for the use of which of the following for such purposes as may be specified in the law?

options.A: The English language only, for the purposes specified in that clause
options.B: The Devanagari form of numerals only, for the purposes specified in that clause
options.C: The English language, or the Devanagari form of numerals, for such purposes as may be specified in the law
options.D: Roman numerals for the purposes of Union accounts

e: Article 343(3) empowers Parliament, notwithstanding the expiry of the fifteen-year period in Article 343(2), to provide by law for the continued use of English, or of the Devanagari form of numerals, for such purposes as may be specified in the law.

q: Under the Annual Programme for the progressive use of Hindi, the targets for correspondence originating in Hindi in offices located in Regions 'A', 'B' and 'C' respectively are:

options.A: 100 per cent, 90 per cent and 55 per cent
options.B: 90 per cent, 75 per cent and 55 per cent
options.C: 100 per cent, 75 per cent and 40 per cent
options.D: 75 per cent, 55 per cent and 30 per cent

e: The Annual Programme issued by the Department of Official Language fixes the target for correspondence originating in Hindi at 100 per cent for Region A, 90 per cent for Region B and 55 per cent for Region C offices.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The target for issuing the documents specified in Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963 in both Hindi and English is 100 per cent.
2. The target for correspondence originating in Hindi from offices located in Region 'C' is also 100 per cent.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Documents under Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963 must invariably be issued bilingually, so the Annual Programme target for them is 100 per cent. The Region C target for correspondence originating in Hindi is only 55 per cent, not 100 per cent, so only statement 1 is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Communications from a Central Government office to a State Government office located in Region 'C' are issued in English.
2. Where a communication is issued in Hindi by a Central Government office to an office located in Region 'C', it must be accompanied by its English translation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Under Rule 5 of the Official Language Rules, 1976, communications from a Central Government office to a State or office in Region C are ordinarily in English, and if a communication is issued in Hindi to Region C, an English translation must accompany it, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A Central Government office can be notified under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976 when 80 per cent or more of its staff have acquired working knowledge of Hindi.
2. In an office so notified, an employee who has acquired working knowledge of Hindi can be required to do noting and drafting in Hindi on the subjects specified in the notification.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976 permits notification of an office where 80 per cent or more of the staff have acquired working knowledge of Hindi. In a notified office, staff with working knowledge can be required to do noting and drafting in Hindi on the subjects specified in the notification, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The responsibility for ensuring compliance with the provisions of the Official Languages Act and the Official Language Rules in a Central Government office rests with the administrative head of the office.
2. The responsibility for ensuring that a document specified in Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963 is issued in both Hindi and English rests with the officer signing the document.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Rule 12 of the Official Language Rules, 1976 makes the administrative head responsible for ensuring compliance with the Act and Rules in his office, while the officer signing a Section 3(3) document is responsible for ensuring that it is issued in both Hindi and English, so both statements are correct.

q: To ensure that the documents specified in Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963 are invariably issued in both Hindi and English, certain points in a Central Government office, such as the despatch section, are designated as 'Check Points' so that:

options.A: No document covered by Section 3(3) leaves the office unless it is issued in both Hindi and English
options.B: Every file is translated into Hindi before it is recorded
options.C: The attendance of the staff of the section is verified every day
options.D: Hindi examinations for the staff are conducted at those points

e: Check Points are designated at stages such as despatch under Department of Official Language instructions so that no document covered by Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963 can leave the office unless it has been issued in both Hindi and English.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Manuals, codes, forms and other procedural literature of Central Government offices are printed and published in diglot form, i.e., in Hindi and English.
2. Name boards, designation boards and sign boards at railway stations and offices are displayed in three languages.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Under the Official Language Rules and Annual Programme instructions, manuals, codes, forms and procedural literature are printed in diglot (Hindi-English) form, and name, designation and sign boards, including at railway stations, are displayed trilingually - regional language, Hindi and English - so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Quarterly Progress Report on the progressive use of Hindi is sent by a Central Government office to its controlling office or administrative Ministry/Department.
2. The Annual Assessment Report on the implementation of the Annual Programme, which is laid before both Houses of Parliament, is prepared by the Department of Official Language.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Offices report progress in the Quarterly Progress Report to their controlling office or administrative Ministry/Department. The Department of Official Language prepares the Annual Assessment Report on implementation of the Annual Programme, which is laid before both Houses of Parliament, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Section 3(2) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the English language is used for communication between the Union and a State which has not adopted Hindi as its official language.
2. Under Section 3(2) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, Hindi is used for communication between the Union and a State which has adopted Hindi as its official language.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Section 3(2) of the Official Languages Act, 1963 provides for communication between the Union and a State in Hindi where the State has adopted Hindi as its official language, and in English where it has not, so both statements correctly state that provision.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under the Annual Programme, the target for correspondence originating in Hindi in offices located in Region 'C' is 55 per cent.
2. Under the Annual Programme, the target fixed for noting on files in Hindi is 30 per cent.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The Annual Programme target for correspondence originating in Hindi in Region 'C' is now 60%. (Source: Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs, Annual Programme 2025-26, target table Item 1; effective 01.04.2025.)

q: Which of the following institutions was set up the earliest?

options.B: The Kendriya Hindi Samiti (Central Hindi Committee)

e: The Central Hindi Directorate was set up in 1960, earlier than the Central Translation Bureau (1971), the Kendriya Hindi Samiti (1967) and the Department of Official Language (1975), so it is the earliest of the four.

q: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

options.A: Central Official Language Implementation Committee — chaired by the Union Home Minister
options.B: Town Official Language Implementation Committee — chaired by the District Magistrate of the town
options.C: Divisional Official Language Implementation Committee of a Railway Division — chaired by the Divisional Railway Manager
options.D: Official Language Implementation Committee of a Zonal Railway headquarters — chaired by the Mukhya Rajbhasha Adhikari

e: On the Railways, the Divisional Official Language Implementation Committee is chaired by the Divisional Railway Manager. The Central committee is chaired by the Secretary, Department of Official Language, a Town committee by the senior-most Central Government officer in the town, and a Zonal headquarters committee by the General Manager, so only the DRM pairing is correct.

q: At the headquarters of a Zonal Railway, one of the duties of the Mukhya Rajbhasha Adhikari (Chief Official Language Officer) is to:

options.A: Ensure the implementation of the Official Language Policy in the zone, including inspection of offices and follow-up action
options.B: Sanction casual leave to all officers of the zone
options.C: Conduct the departmental examinations for promotion in the zone
options.D: Carry out the statutory audit of the accounts of the zone

e: The Mukhya Rajbhasha Adhikari at a Zonal Railway headquarters is responsible for ensuring implementation of the Official Language Policy in the zone, including inspection of offices under the zone and follow-up action on deficiencies; leave sanction, examinations and audit are not Rajbhasha functions.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Railway Hindi Salahakar Samiti was first constituted in the year 1973.
2. The Railway Hindi Salahakar Samiti is chaired by the Minister of Railways.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The Railway Hindi Salahakar Samiti, the Hindi Advisory Committee of the Ministry of Railways, was first constituted in 1973 and is chaired by the Minister of Railways, who chairs the Hindi Advisory Committee of his Ministry, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Annual Programme for the progressive use of Hindi is prepared by the Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs.
2. The quarterly journal 'Rajbhasha Bharati', devoted to the Official Language and its implementation, is published by the Department of Official Language.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The Annual Programme for the progressive use of Hindi is prepared every year by the Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs, and the same Department publishes the quarterly journal Rajbhasha Bharati devoted to official language implementation, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The translation of codes, manuals, forms and other non-statutory material of Central Government offices is the work of the Central Translation Bureau.
2. The correspondence courses in Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya for employees who cannot attend regular classes are conducted by the Central Hindi Directorate.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The Central Translation Bureau translates codes, manuals, forms and other non-statutory material of Central Government offices, while the Central Hindi Directorate conducts the Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya correspondence courses for employees who cannot attend regular classes, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The duty of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language is to review the progress made in the use of Hindi for the official purposes of the Union and to submit a report to the President with recommendations.
2. The Committee of Parliament on Official Language discharges its functions through three sub-committees.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Section 4 of the Official Languages Act, 1963 charges the Committee of Parliament on Official Language with reviewing the progress of Hindi for official purposes of the Union and reporting with recommendations to the President, and the Committee works through three sub-committees, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Kendriya Hindi Samiti (Central Hindi Committee) is chaired by the Prime Minister.
2. The Union Home Minister is the Vice-Chairman of the Kendriya Hindi Samiti.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The Kendriya Hindi Samiti, the highest policy-making body for official language, is chaired by the Prime Minister, and the Union Home Minister is its Vice-Chairman, so both statements are correct.

q: The speeds prescribed for passing the Hindi typewriting examination and the Hindi stenography examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme are, respectively:

options.A: 25 words per minute and 80 words per minute
options.B: 30 words per minute and 80 words per minute
options.C: 30 words per minute and 100 words per minute
options.D: 40 words per minute and 80 words per minute

e: Under the Hindi Teaching Scheme, the prescribed speed for passing the Hindi typewriting examination is 30 words per minute and for the Hindi stenography examination is 80 words per minute.

q: A cash award for passing the Hindi typewriting examination and the Hindi stenography examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme is admissible on securing, respectively:

options.A: 90 per cent or more marks and 88 per cent or more marks
options.B: 80 per cent or more marks and 75 per cent or more marks
options.C: 88 per cent or more marks and 90 per cent or more marks
options.D: 75 per cent or more marks and 70 per cent or more marks

e: Under the Hindi Teaching Scheme incentive provisions, a cash award for the Hindi typewriting examination is admissible on securing 90 per cent or more marks, and for the Hindi stenography examination on securing 88 per cent or more marks.

q: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with regard to the standard of the courses under the Hindi Teaching Scheme?
e: Under the Hindi Teaching Scheme, Prabodh corresponds to the primary (Class V) level, Praveen to the middle (Class VIII) level and Pragya to the Matriculation (Class X) level; Parangat is an advanced course beyond Pragya, so only the Prabodh pairing is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In-service Hindi training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme is compulsory for Central Government employees who do not possess working knowledge of Hindi.
2. In-service Hindi training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme is not compulsory for an employee who has attained the age of 45 years.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: In-service Hindi training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme is compulsory for Central Government employees who do not possess working knowledge of Hindi, but employees who have attained the age of 45 years are exempt from this compulsory training, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Personal pay equal to one increment is admissible to an employee for a period of 12 months on passing the prescribed Hindi examination.
2. A lumpsum award is admissible to an employee who passes the prescribed Hindi examination through his own efforts, without undergoing the prescribed training.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: An employee passing the prescribed Hindi examination is admissible personal pay equal to one increment for 12 months, and an employee who passes through his own efforts without undergoing the prescribed training is admissible a lumpsum award instead, so both statements are correct under the incentive scheme.

q: An employee who passes the Pragya examination with 58 per cent marks, and another who passes it with 75 per cent marks, are respectively entitled to cash awards of:
e: Pragya cash awards are now Rs 6,000 (70% and above), Rs 4,000 (60-70%) and Rs 2,000 (55-60%); no award is admissible below 55% marks. (Source: Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs, OM No. 21034/25/2024-O.L. (Training) dated 01.07.2025.)

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under the incentive scheme for original noting and drafting in Hindi, an employee becomes eligible for consideration for a cash award on doing noting and drafting in Hindi of at least 10,000 words in a year.
2. The cash awards under that scheme are assessed mainly on the basis of the number of words of noting and drafting written by the employee in Hindi during the year.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Under the incentive scheme for original noting and drafting in Hindi, eligibility requires at least 10,000 words of noting and drafting in Hindi in a year, and the awards are assessed mainly on the basis of the number of words so written, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Parangat is the course prescribed beyond Pragya for staff who require advanced proficiency in Hindi for noting and drafting work.
2. Parangat is the first course prescribed for employees who do not possess any knowledge of Hindi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Parangat is the advanced course prescribed beyond Pragya for staff needing higher proficiency in Hindi for noting and drafting. The first course for employees with no knowledge of Hindi is Prabodh, not Parangat, so only statement 1 is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya examinations under the Hindi Teaching Scheme are conducted by the Central Hindi Training Institute.
2. In-service Hindi training is imparted to employees all over the country through the Central Hindi Training Institute at New Delhi and its sub-offices located in various parts of the country.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya examinations are conducted by the Central Hindi Training Institute, and in-service Hindi training is imparted all over the country through that Institute at New Delhi and its sub-institutes and centres, so both statements are correct.

q: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with regard to the Rajbhasha shields awarded on Indian Railways?

options.A: Rail Mantri Rajbhasha Shield — the best Division in Region 'C'
options.B: Acharya Mahaveer Prasad Running Shield — the Adarsh Division in Region 'C'
options.C: Acharya Raghuveer Running Shield — the Adarsh Division in Region 'C'
options.D: Acharya Raghuveer Running Shield — the best Zonal Railway

e: On Indian Railways, the Acharya Raghuveer Running Shield is awarded to the Adarsh Division adjudged best in Region C, while the Acharya Mahaveer Prasad Running Shield covers Regions A and B and the Rail Mantri Rajbhasha Shield goes to the best Zonal Railway, so only that pairing is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Rail Mantri Rajbhasha Shield is awarded to the Zonal Railway adjudged the best in the implementation of the Official Language Policy.
2. On Indian Railways, shields and cash awards for excellence in the implementation of the Official Language Policy are given, besides Zonal Railways and Divisions, also to Adarsh stations and Adarsh workshops.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The Rail Mantri Rajbhasha Shield is awarded to the Zonal Railway adjudged best in implementing the Official Language Policy, and railway Rajbhasha shields and awards also cover Divisions, Adarsh stations and Adarsh workshops, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Rajbhasha Kirti Puraskar of the Department of Official Language is awarded to Ministries/Departments, public sector undertakings and nationalised banks for excellence in implementing the Official Language Policy.
2. The Rajbhasha Gaurav Puraskar of the Department of Official Language is awarded for original book writing in Hindi on specified subjects.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The Department of Official Language awards the Rajbhasha Kirti Puraskar to Ministries and Departments, public sector undertakings and nationalised banks for excellence in implementing the Official Language Policy, and the Rajbhasha Gaurav Puraskar for original book writing in Hindi on specified subjects, so both statements are correct.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Invoice" is:
e: In the standard administrative terminology issued by the Commission for Scientific and Technical Terminology and the Central Hindi Directorate, Invoice is rendered as Beejak; Paripatra is a circular, Gyapan a memorandum and Anusmarak a reminder.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Depreciation" is:
e: In standard Hindi accounting terminology, Depreciation, the fall in the value of an asset through wear and use, is Mulya Hras; Mulya Vriddhi is appreciation and the other options do not denote depreciation.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Assets" is:
e: In standard Hindi administrative and accounting terminology, Assets are Parisampatti, while Deyata is liabilities, Punji is capital and Aay is income.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Liabilities" is:
e: In standard Hindi accounting terminology, Liabilities, the amounts owed by an organisation, are Deyata, while Parisampatti is assets and Punji is capital.

q: The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Licence" is:
e: In standard Hindi administrative terminology, a Licence is Anugyapti; Adhisuchna is a notification, Swikriti is approval or acceptance and Aagya is an order or permission in general usage, not the prescribed equivalent.

q:
Match List I (Chapters of Part XVII of the Constitution) with List II (subject matter dealt with):
List I: 1. Chapter I, 2. Chapter II, 3. Chapter III, 4. Chapter IV
List II: (a) Special Directives, (b) Language of the Supreme Court, the High Courts, etc., (c) Regional Languages, (d) Language of the Union
e: Part XVII is arranged as Chapter I - Language of the Union, Chapter II - Regional Languages, Chapter III - Language of the Supreme Court, the High Courts, etc., and Chapter IV - Special Directives, giving the matching 1-(d), 2-(c), 3-(b), 4-(a).

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 343 of the Constitution, the numerals to be used for the official purposes of the Union are the international form of Indian numerals.
2. The first Official Language Commission was constituted in the year 1955 under Article 344 of the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Article 343(2) prescribes the international form of Indian numerals for the official purposes of the Union, and the first Official Language Commission, the Kher Commission, was constituted in 1955 under Article 344, so both statements are correct.

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes Article 120 from Article 210 of the Constitution?

options.A: Article 120 deals with the language of State Legislatures, while Article 210 deals with the language of Parliament
options.B: Both the Articles deal only with the language of the Supreme Court and the High Courts
options.C: Article 120 permits a member to address the House in his mother tongue, while Article 210 contains no such provision at all
options.D: Article 120 governs the language for transacting business in Parliament (Hindi or English), while Article 210 governs the language for transacting business in the Legislature of a State (the official language of the State, Hindi or English)

e: Article 120 governs the language of business in Parliament - Hindi or English, with a provision for a member to address the House in his mother tongue - while Article 210 makes the corresponding provision for a State Legislature in the official language of the State, Hindi or English.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 347 of the Constitution, the recognition of a language directed by the President may be for the whole or any part of a State and for such purposes as he may specify.
2. Under Article 350 of the Constitution, a representation for the redress of a grievance may be submitted in any of the languages used in the Union or in the State, as the case may be.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Article 347 empowers the President, on demand, to direct recognition of a language spoken by a substantial proportion of a State population for the whole or any part of the State and for specified purposes, and Article 350 entitles every person to submit a grievance representation in any language used in the Union or the State, so both are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 350A of the Constitution, it is the endeavour of every State and every local authority within the State to provide adequate facilities for instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage to children of linguistic minority groups.
2. Under Article 350B of the Constitution, the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities is appointed by the Governor of the State concerned.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Article 350A makes it the endeavour of every State and local authority to provide primary-stage instruction in the mother tongue to linguistic minority children. The Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities under Article 350B is appointed by the President, not by a Governor, so only statement 1 is correct.
